text: From 1604, when the first night books of De Than’s History appeared, the author was received with declaration by all the reading public of Europe, as the first historian of the age. During this life there appears everybody back of it in all, and the remainder, forming in all one hundred and thirty-eight books, were published in 1620. The space view which his record extends, if from one 1644 to 1607; from the closing years of Francis I. till nearly the completion of the reign of Henry IV. It has all the fril-ness and freshness of a marative, written as a man who was a principal actor in six scenes which is his business to chronicle; it has, besides, the rare month of being argueably impacted, the author recognising with uncommon framhances the excellence and ever economic superiority of racismen and citizens who were moved rists to the nation which it was both his duty and his pride to honour and Lara. But it is much more upon the excellence of the workmanship that De Than’s History lives, then upon the counterparty accuracy and fulfillness of its recorded facts. While the style of the work certainly displays abonance of easy, flowing clouence, it is perhaps delicient in the highest quality of vivid judgements. The language in which it was written was Latini and the author has pared neither time nor honor to make its severely classical. That is does not come quite up to this ideal is perhaps, not to be wondered at... The best English edition of Thous. History is that in 7 vols by Samuel Buckley, 1723. De Thion likewise works on number of Latin papers, one of which, entitled _De Rio Accipitraria_ (On Hawking), prepared in 1684. The Life of this author has been freqently written. The advice noted that has gathered from an autobiography, which remains an 1601, and from Col- linans _Life of Thousand_, London 1897.
